products.name: Workday AI
products.note: HR and finance AI; skills-based talent; predictive analytics; sensitive HR data exposure

profile_text.body:
Workday is a publicly traded enterprise software company, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Pleasanton, CA, that sells cloud-based applications for human resources, finance, and IT. The company trades on the ticker WDAY and reported revenue of $9,552,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing. Its SEC CIK is 0001327811.

The company describes its core offering as an enterprise AI platform and markets a product called Workday AI, which covers HR and finance workflows, skills-based talent management, and predictive analytics. The site also references a collaboration with Sana and promotes what it calls agentic AI, describing agents that can find, build, act, and automate across HR, finance, and IT processes. The site frames these capabilities as turning AI into measurable business returns driven by trust, agility, and data readiness, though the company's own product notes flag that the platform handles sensitive HR data.

Workday faces a notable volume of litigation, with nine federal cases on record across multiple districts including the Eastern District of California, the Northern District of California, the Northern District of Georgia, the District of Colorado, the District of Maryland, and the Eastern District of Virginia. Several cases share the Meckfessel Poletti name and others include Williams v. Workday, Elias v. Workday, Hill v. Workday, and Doe v. Workday. The site's law exposure data associates 161 California-related legal data points with the company.
